svg.title: Seccomp: a system call filter in front of the kernel
svg.desc: Step 1, a process such as a model server makes system calls, some normal and some from injected attacker code. Step 2, the seccomp filter, a small BPF program, checks each call's number and raw argument values but cannot follow pointers to read paths or buffers. Step 3, allowed calls run in the kernel. Step 4, denied calls fail with an error or kill the process. Step 5, a profile is built by recording a test run in log mode, then allowing only the recorded calls and denying the rest. Step 6, Kubernetes offers three profile types: RuntimeDefault, the runtime's default; Localhost, a custom file on the node; and Unconfined, no filter, which is the Kubernetes default unless the kubelet's seccomp-default setting is on. Step 7 shows the other layers that seccomp works with.
